summary: The enterprise AI API landscape in 2026 is dominated by hyperscaler aggregation platforms that let corporations access multiple foundation models through a single managed API while keeping data inside their existing cloud boundary. There is no single winner — the best fit is usually dictated by an organization's existing cloud footprint (AWS, Microsoft, or Google), with data-platform players like Snowflake and Databricks and specialists like IBM watsonx, Oracle, and Cloudflare addressing specific governance, data-gravity, and edge needs. Throughput units, model availability, and compliance certifications vary widely and do not convert cleanly across platforms.
why_enterprises_use_aggregators: Data residency and privacy: inference runs within the company's own cloud tenant/VPC so prompts and outputs never leave the governed environment or get used to train third-party models.
Compliance and certifications: aggregators inherit the cloud provider's SOC 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, FedRAMP, and regional (EU/GDPR) attestations, satisfying auditors far faster than direct vendor APIs.
Model choice and avoiding lock-in: one API surface gives access to Claude, Llama, Mistral, Gemini, GPT, and open models, so teams can swap or benchmark models without re-architecting.
Consolidated billing and existing contracts: usage draws down existing cloud committed-spend agreements (EDPs/MACC), simplifying procurement and leveraging negotiated discounts.
Enterprise controls and data gravity: integrated IAM, audit logging, private networking, and co-location with corporate data (warehouses, lakes) reduce egress cost and security surface.

platforms.name: Azure OpenAI Service (Azure AI Foundry)
platforms.pricing: Pay-as-you-go per 1K/1M tokens plus Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) for reserved capacity; billed through Azure, drawable against MACC commitments.
key_features: Private VPC/VNet integration and Private Link
Data not used to train base models
platforms.best_for: Microsoft-first enterprises wanting the deepest OpenAI/GPT access with Office/Copilot and Azure governance integration.

platforms.name: AWS Bedrock
platforms.pricing: On-demand per-token pricing plus Provisioned Throughput for reserved capacity; serverless, billed through AWS and usable against EDP commitments.
key_features: AWS IAM as source of truth
platforms.best_for: AWS-native enterprises wanting the widest choice of models (especially Claude) behind one API with IAM-centric governance.

platforms.name: Google Vertex AI Model Garden
platforms.pricing: Pay-per-token or per-character; GSU (Generative Scale Unit) reserved throughput — e.g., 25 GSUs of Gemini 2.5 Flash yields roughly 67,250 tokens/sec sustained; billed through GCP.
key_features: VPC Service Controls and Private Service Connect
platforms.best_for: GCP-heavy and data/ML-centric organizations wanting native Gemini plus multimodal (Imagen/Veo) and MLOps tooling.

platforms.name: Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based, billed in Snowflake credits per token/function call; runs on existing Snowflake compute contract.
key_features: Inference next to governed data (no data movement)
platforms.best_for: Enterprises with data gravity in Snowflake wanting LLMs applied directly to governed warehouse data.

platforms.name: IBM watsonx.ai
platforms.pricing: Resource Unit (RU) consumption pricing; available as SaaS, on-prem, or hybrid via Cloud Pak for Data.
key_features: On-prem and hybrid deployment for data sovereignty
platforms.best_for: Regulated enterprises (finance, government, healthcare) needing on-prem/hybrid deployment, strong governance, and IP indemnification.

platforms.name: Databricks Mosaic AI
platforms.pricing: Consumption-based DBUs via Model Serving and Foundation Model APIs on existing Databricks contract.
platforms.best_for: Data engineering and ML teams on the lakehouse wanting to fine-tune and serve models next to governed data.

platforms.name: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI
platforms.pricing: Per-character/token or dedicated AI cluster (reserved units); billed through OCI, usable with Universal Credits.
key_features: Deep integration with Oracle Database/Fusion apps
platforms.best_for: Oracle database and ERP/Fusion application customers needing GenAI within OCI and sovereign deployments.

platforms.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
platforms.pricing: Usage-based per neuron/request on the pay-as-you-go Workers platform; low-cost, serverless at the edge.
key_features: AI Gateway for caching, rate-limiting, and multi-provider routing
platforms.best_for: Developers and enterprises needing low-latency, globally distributed inference and a lightweight multi-provider AI gateway.
